West Ham United Dismiss Head Coach Nuno Espirito Santo After 14 Months

West Ham Make Management Change

West Ham United have announced the departure of head coach Nuno Espirito Santo following a challenging start to the EFL Championship season. The 52-year-old manager spent 14 months at the club, having taken charge in September 2025 following the departure of Graham Potter. During his tenure, the team suffered relegation from the Premier League at the end of the previous campaign.

Alongside Espirito Santo, assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also left the London club. A club statement indicated that the board of directors conducted a thorough review of the season's opening matches and concluded that a change was necessary to keep the club's objectives on track.

Temporary Leadership and Recent Form

Mark Noble, Steve Potts, and Gerard Prenderville have been appointed to take temporary charge of the squad ahead of their upcoming Championship fixture against Cardiff City.

  • Current Standing: West Ham currently sit eighth in the Championship table.
  • Recent Results: The team has secured two victories in their last six matches, suffering consecutive home defeats against Southampton (3-2) and West Bromwich Albion (3-1).
  • Promotion Expectations: Despite being considered early favourites for automatic promotion, the side trails league leaders Middlesbrough by six points.

Historical Context and Managerial Turnover

The decision highlights ongoing managerial instability at the London Stadium. West Ham are now searching for their fourth permanent manager since David Moyes departed in May 2024. Previous permanent appointments during this period include Julen Lopetegui and Graham Potter, both of whose tenures ended prematurely amid struggles in the top flight.

Although Espirito Santo remained in charge following relegation, the current second-tier campaign began with a winless streak in their opening three matches. While a brief resurgence in September saw the side climb the table following a series of convincing wins, inconsistent form in recent weeks prompted the board to make a change. The club confirmed that the process to recruit a new head coach is already underway.
